title: Polynomial-time indicators define a language in P
statement: Let $V$ be a language of bit strings. If the function that sends each bit string $x$ to the one-bit string indicating whether $x\in V$ is polynomial-time computable, then $V$ belongs to $\mathsf{P}$.
hypotheses_covered: V is a language of bit strings
the one-bit indicator function of V is polynomial-time computable
replaced:
Let $V \subseteq \{0,1\}^{*}$ be a language and let $\mathbf{1}_V(x)$ be the bit
$1$ if $x \in V$ and $0$ otherwise. If the map sending a binary string $x$ to the
one-bit string $\mathbf{1}_V(x)$ is polynomial-time computable, i.e.\ some finite
multi-tape Turing machine over the binary alphabet computes it within $D(n+1)^d$
steps on every input of length $n$ for some constants $D, d$, then
$V \in \mathsf{P}$.
